On the road
Where the letters were written, where they went, and the roads they travelled.
ON THE MAP
Where the letters went
Toggle a collection to see the places its letters were sent.
The cities, regions and people that received Paul's letters, as the letters themselves name them.

Five places proposed for the letter's first readers. None is named in the letter; each pin shows a view and who held it, not a conclusion. Others thought of a Jewish community elsewhere in the East, of Gentile Christians, or of no single church at all. Hebrews 13:24 [28]

1 Peter names its readers' regions in the order Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, Bithynia — though Pontus and Bithynia were one Roman province, they stand at opposite ends of the list. Hort took the order to follow the route of the man carrying the letter; Easton thought it the order that would occur to someone writing from Babylon on the Euphrates. Bigg notes that, read loosely, the list covers the whole of Asia Minor except the south coast. Pins mark the site's region centres, not boundaries. 1 Peter 1:1 Acts 2:9 [19][20]
None of the three letters names a place. Early tradition sets John at Ephesus late in his life, and the letters are usually linked with the churches of the province of Asia around it.[25][26]

Romans: where it was written

Corinth, or its port Cenchrea, by almost every account. Paul commends Phebe of the church at Cenchrea, sends greetings from Gaius, his host (a Gaius of Corinth appears in 1 Corinthians), and from Erastus, the city's chamberlain. Moule (ISBE) names Corinth "with confidence"; Easton and Schaff agree. The old note printed after the letter in the KJV ("from Corinthus") is a later scribal addition, not Scripture, though here it agrees with the usual view. Romans 16:1 Romans 16:23 1 Corinthians 1:14 [19][5]
CARRIED
How Paul's letters travelled
Each of Paul's letters, from where it was written to where it was sent.
Romans: from Corinth to Rome.
1 Corinthians: from Ephesus to Corinth.
2 Corinthians: from Macedonia to Corinth and all Achaia.
Galatians: from Ephesus to The churches of Galatia.
THE ROADS
Paul's journeys and Silvanus's road
Paul's journeys, the voyage to Rome, and the road Hort suggested for 1 Peter. Play one to draw it leg by leg.

With Barnabas, from Antioch through Cyprus to the cities of southern Asia Minor and back. Places in the order the KJV text of Acts names them; each reference is where the place is first named on that leg. Pairs that Acts names together are shown as separate stops. Ramsay dates it spring 47 to August 49; Robertson 47-48 or 48-49. Acts 13:1–14:28 [10][17]

With Silas, joined by Timothy at Lystra, across to Macedonia and Achaia. Places in the order the KJV text of Acts names them; each reference is where the place is first named on that leg. Pairs that Acts names together are shown as separate stops. Ramsay dates it spring 50 to March 53. Acts 15:36–18:22 [10][17]

The long stay at Ephesus, a return through Macedonia and Greece, and the voyage to Jerusalem with the collection. Places in the order the KJV text of Acts names them; each reference is where the place is first named on that leg. Pairs that Acts names together are shown as separate stops. Ramsay dates it June 53 to May 57. Acts 18:23–21:17 [10][17]

Paul sails as a prisoner after appealing to Caesar, is shipwrecked on Melita and reaches Rome. Places in the order the KJV text of Acts names them; each reference is where the place is first named on that leg. Pairs that Acts names together are shown as separate stops. Ramsay dates it August 59 to February 60. Acts 27:1–28:16 [10]
